claim: Sequential weight edits destroy a reasoning model's general abilities within about a hundred edits, unless the edit is constrained to leave existing knowledge untouched. Supported only if, on a distilled reasoning model, after 100 sequential fact edits, rank-one and meta-learned editors bring average accuracy on five competition-math benchmarks and on three broader reasoning benchmarks (graduate science questions, ARC-Challenge, MMLU-Pro) from above 50% to below 1%, while a null-space-constrained editor stays within 2 points of the unedited model on both averages.

experiments: Set up the benchmark. Setup: weight-editing methods ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L (locate-then-edit), MEND (meta-learned), AdaLoRA and WISE (added parameters); external-memory methods GRACE and SCR (retrieve stored edits and select them as context); all through EasyEdit on Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Llama-2-13B and Qwen3-14B. Data: ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact (counterfactual fact edits) and ELKEN events, converted to fact triples by GPT-4o for the weight editors and given as raw text to memory methods. Answers are generated autoregressively (50 tokens, 1,024 for the reasoning model) instead of teacher-forced, and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judges semantic agreement (96% agreement with humans on 250 samples) for reliability, generalisation, locality and portability. Every edit in a dataset is applied in sequence and the final model evaluated.

Measure general reasoning after editing. Setup: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B after 10 and 100 sequential ZsRE edits; AIME 2024 and 2025, AMC, MATH-500, OlympiadBench, and GPQA-Diamond, ARC-Challenge, MMLU-Pro. Result: math average 53.47 unedited; after 10 / 100 edits 50.73 / 0.00 for ROME, 45.10 / 0.03 for RECT, 0.00 / 0.00 for MEND, 53.92 / 53.12 for AlphaEdit. Broad average 54.24 unedited; 49.05 / 0.00 ROME, 50.37 / 0.00 RECT, 0 / 0 MEND, 53.08 / 52.88 AlphaEdit.

Inspect how edited reasoning models fail. Setup: case analysis of edited DeepSeek-R1-Distill outputs. Result: the edit often makes the model produce the new answer as the next token, but its reasoning trace then reverts to the old fact, fabricates plausible-sounding justifications for the edited answer, or drifts away from the question (qualitative).
